transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, Dr. Smith, I'm Janet. I decided to come in because I keep eating big amounts of food at night even when I’m not really hungry at all. It's just gotten to a point where I know I need some help.
After these episodes of overeating, do you feel a need to do anything to get rid of the calories, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things like throwing up or using laxatives. Instead, I just sit there in the quiet kitchen, staring at the empty pans and wrappers, feeling so heavy and ashamed of myself. I just end up beating myself up over what I've done.
How many days per week, on average, would you say these episodes of eating large amounts of food occur?

For the last several months, it's rare for a week to go by without at least one of those nights happening. On tougher weeks, especially after an emotionally draining day at the food bank or church, it can happen two or three times.
